title: PwD Marking, Postal Ballot and Home Voting
summary: Persons with Disabilities (PwD) can be flagged in the electoral roll via Form 8, and — along with electors above 85 years — may be eligible for postal ballot / home voting via Form 12D submitted at election time.
body:
Two separate steps are involved:

1. Getting marked as PwD in the electoral roll: submit Form 8 (online, at a Voter Service Centre, or via the Saksham ECI application) selecting the PwD-marking option, in one of the disability categories specified by ECI.
2. Requesting home voting at a specific election: once notified as PwD in the roll (or if you are aged 85+), you may submit Form 12D to the Returning Officer within 5 days of that election's notification to request postal ballot / home voting. A polling team then visits your home to collect your vote on a schedule shared with candidates/agents. Postal ballots must reach the Returning Officer by the deadline set for that election (typically 8:00 AM on counting day).

This facility is election-specific — you must apply again (Form 12D) for each election in which you want to use it; PwD-marking on the roll (Form 8) itself is a one-time status update.

sources.title: ECI to facilitate Elderly, PwD and Service Voters via Postal Ballot

caution: Home-voting eligibility age thresholds and the list of PwD categories are set by ECI notification for each election cycle — confirm current thresholds before advising a specific user.
